title: Tyndale laws_regulations record
description: A statute/regulation chunk. Point-in-time filtered: every query filters by date-of-service against effective_date_start/end. Carries the X6 classification (DL-84) so the runtime can voice CATEGORICAL vs CONDITIONAL claims per the calibrated-voice rules, and supports affirmative no-state-law records (DL-81) so the ABSENCE of a state protection is itself retrievable rather than a silent gap.

statute.description: e.g. '29 U.S.C.', '42 U.S.C.', 'Cal. Health & Safety Code'. Null ONLY permitted when document_type is 'no_state_law' (an affirmative 'this jurisdiction has no such statute' record).

section.description: Null ONLY permitted when document_type is 'no_state_law'.

document_type.description: 'no_state_law' is an affirmative record that a jurisdiction lacks a protection in a given area (e.g. no state balance-billing statute reaching self-funded plans); statute/section are null for that type only.

chunk_text.description: The embedded text. Federal statutes/regulations are public domain. For no_state_law records this is the plain-language statement of what protection is absent and what that means for the user.

last_verified_date.description: Set by the Regulation Researcher cron (Phase 5).

x6_classification.description: DL-84. CATEGORICAL: the rule applies flatly once the authority is on point (e.g. ERISA's 180-day appeal window). CONDITIONAL: the protection turns on facts about the encounter that must be established (see checkable_facts) and can be lost (see defeaters).

checkable_facts.description: The encounter facts that must hold for a CONDITIONAL protection to apply (e.g. 'service was non-emergency', 'out-of-network provider at in-network facility'). May be empty ONLY for CATEGORICAL records; enforced non-empty for CONDITIONAL below.

defeaters.description: Facts that defeat an otherwise-applicable protection (e.g. 'valid NSA notice-and-consent obtained', 'plan is ERISA self-funded so state law is preempted'). May be empty.

scope.description: Which coverage populations this authority actually binds, and the ground-ambulance answer (a deliberate required field because ground ambulance is the best-known NSA gap and must never be left implicit).

plan_types_bound.description: The populations this authority reaches. State surprise-billing statutes typically bind only 'state_regulated_commercial' and NOT 'erisa_self_funded'; federal law (NSA, ERISA) may bind 'all' or specific populations.

ground_ambulance_covered.description: Whether this authority's balance-billing protection extends to GROUND ambulance. null means 'not applicable to this record' (e.g. a non-surprise-billing statute); for surprise-billing records it MUST be an explicit boolean — the 51-state seed check enforces non-null.

as_of.description: DL-84. The date the X6 classification / statute snapshot was verified by the authoring reviewer. Surfaced in citations so the model can state how current the classification is. Often equal to last_verified_date, but tracked separately because the classification review date can differ from the text-verification date.

allOf.description: statute + section are null-able ONLY for no_state_law; every other document_type requires real strings.
CONDITIONAL records must enumerate at least one checkable fact; CATEGORICAL records may leave checkable_facts empty.

examples.parent_part: Part 2560 — Rules and Regulations for Administration and Enforcement
examples.chunk_text: A group health plan's claims procedure must allow a claimant at least 180 days following receipt of an adverse benefit determination within which to appeal the determination. The plan must provide a full and fair review of the claim and the adverse determination.

This state has no statute protecting patients from balance billing by out-of-network GROUND ambulance providers. Ground ambulance is also excluded from the federal No Surprises Act, so an out-of-network ground-ambulance balance bill is not prohibited by either federal or state law here.
